subject: history
title: From Poland to Pearl Harbor 1939-1941
welcome_lead: Two years that turned regional conflicts into a true world war — follow the path from Warsaw to Hawaii.
meta_desc: IBDP History Move to Global War Adventure 3: 1939-1941, from the invasion of Poland to Pearl Harbor.
final_note: You have closed the inter-war story. From here begins the global conflict of WWII.

concepts.def: Non-aggression treaty between Nazi Germany and the USSR with secret protocols dividing Eastern Europe.
German invasion that began WWII in Europe.
Combined-arms 'lightning war' tactics used by Germany in 1939-41.
Aerial campaign in which the RAF resisted the Luftwaffe over the United Kingdom.
German invasion of the Soviet Union, opening the largest theatre of the war.
Japanese surprise attack on the US Pacific Fleet that brought the United States into the war.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact of 23 August 1939 cleared the way for Germany's invasion of Poland on 1 September; Britain and France declared war on 3 September. The USSR invaded eastern Poland on 17 September, and seized the Baltic States, Bessarabia and parts of Finland. Blitzkrieg conquests of Denmark, Norway, the Low Countries and France followed in 1940.

After the fall of France in June 1940 Britain stood alone in Europe. The Battle of Britain (July-October 1940) prevented invasion. The Blitz, the Lend-Lease Act (March 1941) and the Atlantic Charter (August 1941) symbolised US-British cooperation short of belligerence.

Operation Barbarossa was launched on 22 June 1941, ending the Nazi-Soviet partnership. Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, simultaneous with assaults on the Philippines, Malaya and Hong Kong, drew the United States into the war. Germany declared war on the US four days later, finalising a truly global conflict.
